claims.text: Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi and CrCoNi can both crystallize as single-phase FCC solid solutions.
All relevant equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after identical thermomechanical processing.
Mn is magnetically frustrated in CrMnFeCoNi because its preferred antiferromagnetic alignment cannot be fully satisfied among ferromagnetic Ni, Co, and Fe and antiferromagnetic Cr.
Mn-induced magnetic frustration alters the local electronic environment.
Mn-induced magnetic frustration increases the effective stacking-fault energy of the quinary alloy.
The equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy has an intermediate stacking-fault energy of approximately 25–30 mJ/m2.
Stacking-fault energy controls whether FCC alloys deform predominantly by perfect-dislocation slip, mechanical twinning, or strain-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation.
Increasing stacking-fault energy suppresses stacking-fault nucleation, twinning, and FCC-to-HCP transformation.
Magnetically frustrated Mn eliminates the FCC-HCP energy difference found in CrCoNi.

CrCoNi has a lower-energy HCP phase and undergoes a deformation-triggered FCC-to-HCP transformation that is absent from the parent quinary and the other equiatomic ternary derivatives considered in the evidence.
The FCC-to-HCP transformation in CrCoNi is triggered by dislocation slip and interactions with internal boundaries.
All Mn-reduced or Mn-free quaternary and ternary subsets have lower effective stacking-fault energy than quinary CrMnFeCoNi.
Relative to the quinary alloy, Mn-reduced or Mn-free quaternary and ternary subsets will exhibit more twinning.
Relative to the quinary alloy, Mn-reduced or Mn-free quaternary and ternary subsets will be more prone to FCC-to-HCP transformation.
Changes in twinning and phase transformation will produce measurable differences in yield strength, strain hardening, and ductility.
CrCoNi has a superior combination of strength and plastic deformation relative to CrMnFeCoNi.

contradictions.description: The boundary requires the microstructure to remain FCC during deformation, while the mechanism and predictions explicitly allow an FCC-to-HCP transformation and the experiment is designed to detect that transformation.

The specimens are described as equiatomic subsets while Mn is said to be systematically reduced. In an equiatomic Mn-containing quaternary or ternary subset, Mn would be 25 or 33.3 at.% rather than reduced from the quinary value of 20 at.%; only complete Mn elimination is consistent with both descriptions.
